name: Norfolk Southern
description: Norfolk Southern is a Class I railroad with about 19,100 route miles in 22 eastern states and Washington, DC, hauling merchandise (63% of revenue: agriculture, chemicals, metals, autos), intermodal containers (25%) and coal (12%). Customers pay per carload or container, so revenue is volume times revenue per unit plus fuel surcharge; it owns its track, so profitability is measured by the operating ratio (64.2% in 2025). Its biggest single event is the agreed acquisition by Union Pacific (merger agreement July 28, 2025, subject to Surface Transportation Board approval, $2.5B termination fee), and the 2023 East Palestine derailment still produces legal and environmental costs and insurance recoveries.

gics.note: Conventional GICS sector and sub-industry as listed in Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies), read 2026-10-01; industry group and industry are not shown there. SEC SIC 4011 (Railroads, Line-Haul Operating).

hq.note: 650 West Peachtree Street NW, Atlanta, GA (10-K cover)

employees.note: average 19,400 during 2025; about 80% of railroad employees covered by collective bargaining agreements

businessLines.name: Merchandise (agriculture/forest/consumer, chemicals, metals/construction, automotive)
businessLines.how: Per-carload freight charges plus fuel surcharge on a wide mix of industrial and consumer freight; pricing and mix drove 3% growth in 2025.
businessLines.description: Agriculture, forest and consumer products $2,538M; chemicals $2,206M; metals and construction $1,724M; automotive $1,216M. 2.3 million carloads in 2025.

businessLines.name: Intermodal
businessLines.how: Per-container or per-trailer rail charges; sensitive to import volumes and truck competition.
businessLines.description: Domestic and international containers and trailers handled for intermodal marketing companies, steamship lines and premium customers; 4.1 million units in 2025.

businessLines.name: Coal
businessLines.how: Per-ton and per-carload charges; volume follows power-plant burn and export steel/coal demand.
businessLines.description: 78.0 million tons (0.7 million carloads) to 18 directly served coal-fired power plants plus export, metallurgical and industrial customers.
